<thought>Based on the measurements, the simplest topology that matches all three resistance values is a series connection of two resistors between X1 and X2 with the intermediate node N_b1. The measured resistances are exactly the values of the individual series resistors (5 Ω and 13.333 Ω) and their sum (18.333 Ω). The third resistor does not affect the given measurements; we can place it as a dangling resistor from N_b1 to a reference node (e.g., GND). The note that “one is twice than the other” can be satisfied by making this third resistor twice the smallest resistor (2 × 5 Ω = 10 Ω). 

Thus the circuit topology is:
- R1 = 5 Ω between X1 and N_b1
- R2 = 13.333 Ω between N_b1 and X2
- R3 = 10 Ω between N_b1 and GND (does not affect the measured terminals)
